finding.nature_justification: Per Patch §1.3: Local if Finding涉及的对象/资源/调用全部在当前类内部，可通过本类代码自证。The Claim concerns OrderService.Save method body (OrderService.cs:198-239) and its consecutive ExecuteCommandAsync calls (OrderService.cs:226-237). Whether the method carries a transaction attribute (line 197-198), the class inherits a transactional base (line 36), and whether the method body contains explicit UseTransaction/BeginTran/using-transaction-block (lines 198-239) are all observable within OrderService.cs alone. No cross-class or cross-module evidence is required for Claim verification. Regional was not entered because no interface/dependency/继承链 reference must be resolved across a class boundary to falsify the Claim. Systemic was not entered because the Finding does not require crossing Service↔Repository↔Provider layers or modules. Result: Local.

claim_gate_justification.fq3: Two independent agents reading OrderService.cs:198-239 will agree on the presence/absence of transaction attributes and transaction code without semantic interpretation. No free-text modifiers (合理/适当/尽量/更好) in Claim wording.

evidence.snippet:
[HttpPost("{id}")]
    public async Task Save(string id, [FromBody] OrderCrInput input)
evidence.rationale: Direct Level 1 observation: only [HttpPost] attribute precedes Save; no [UnitOfWork] or any transaction attribute is present. This alone makes any transaction-wrapping claim via attribute falsifiable from this file.

Direct Level 1 observation: lines 226-230 contain five sequential _repository.AsSugarClient().ExecuteCommandAsync() calls. Each is its own auto-commit SqlSugar call. No UseTransaction/BeginTran/try-catch-rollback wrapper is visible inside this if-block. If any single call throws, the previous ones have already committed.
Direct Level 1 observation: lines 235-237 contain three sequential Insertable.ExecuteCommandAsync() calls. Same pattern: no transaction wrapper, each call auto-commits.

Direct Level 1 observation: class declaration shows OrderService inherits IDynamicApiController and ITransient directly. Neither parent provides a transactional hook (IDynamicApiController is a routing marker, ITransient is a lifetime marker per JNPF dependency-injection convention). Therefore no base-class implicit transaction is in play. NOTE: the scenario's 设计文档摘录 claimed Scoped registration; that excerpt is unverified (scenario marks it so) and contradicts the actual ITransient declaration — the code is the only source of truth.

Supplementary Level 1 observation: csproj references JNPF.Common.Core, JNPF.Systems.Interfaces, JNPF.WorkFlow.Interfaces, JNPF.Extend.Interfaces. UnitOfWork is in framework/JNPF and not directly referenced here, but may be transitively pulled via Common.Core. Used only to argue single-point feasibility (the [UnitOfWork] mechanism, defined elsewhere, can be applied to Save without crossing contract — but reading UnitOfWorkAttribute.cs itself would require Scope=1 and exceed S=0; out of Local budget).

five_tuple.claim: OrderService.Save (OrderService.cs:198-239) executes multiple sequential Deleteable/Insertable/Updateable.ExecuteCommandAsync() calls (OrderService.cs:226-230 if-branch; OrderService.cs:235-237 else-branch) without transaction wrapping, such that an intermediate failure leaves prior steps persisted (order/entry/receivable data inconsistency).
five_tuple.evidence: (a) OrderService.cs:197-198 — Save method has only [HttpPost] attribute, no transaction attribute. (b) OrderService.cs:226-230 — five sequential _repository.AsSugarClient().ExecuteCommandAsync() calls inside the if-branch, no UseTransaction/BeginTran wrapper. (c) OrderService.cs:235-237 — three sequential Insertable.ExecuteCommandAsync() calls inside the else-branch, same pattern. (d) OrderService.cs:36 — class implements ITransient and IDynamicApiController directly; no transactional base class. (e) OrderService.cs:198-239 — method body contains no try/catch rollback pattern that would manually compensate for missing transaction. All evidence is Level 1 static code direct observation.
five_tuple.impact: If Claim成立 (no transaction wrapping): each ExecuteCommandAsync() auto-commits; an exception at line 230 (e.g., unique-key violation on the Updateable) leaves lines 226-229 persisted → order/entry/receivable partially updated and inconsistent. Decision = GO: real data-integrity bug, single-point fix feasible by wrapping lines 226-237 in a SqlSugar UseTransaction or applying a [UnitOfWork] attribute (single method, single responsibility, no contract expansion). If Claim不成立 (transaction wrapping present somewhere): Decision = STOP, no fix needed. The dichotomy is sharp under the local evidence.

(3) Impact chain complete — 成立→GO (single-point fix by [UnitOfWork]/UseTransaction), 不成立→STOP (no fix). (4) Decision unique given local evidence — five-tuple yields single GO; the only way to flip would be discovering a hidden transaction mechanism outside OrderService.cs, which would require Scope=1 and exceeds the Local budget S=0. (5) Confidence = High (Level 1 static code, file:line direct correspondence to Claim). Per §3.1 priority, STOP-1 fires before STOP-2 (Decision Stable would also hold under S=0 since CrossLayer CT is non-acquirable within budget) and STOP-3 (Budget would exhaust at depth=1 only after Decision is already made).
